nodes.description: Consolidation of eligible patients in remission is the recommended standard. What the EBMT registry actually resolves is narrower than a transplant-versus-no-transplant comparison, which it did not make: among transplanted patients, myeloablative conditioning - ideally total-body-irradiation based - outperformed reduced-intensity conditioning, and did so *independently of* being in first complete remission, age and performance score. So the conditioning intensity, not merely the graft-versus-tumour effect, carries that difference. The same analysis found one-year outcomes comparable between allogeneic and autologous transplant, and offers autologous transplant for patients ineligible for myeloablative allografting.

nodes.description: Leptomeningeal involvement is characteristically occult: patients are usually neurologically asymptomatic, so it is missed unless cerebrospinal fluid is examined deliberately, and it most often becomes apparent at relapse. That combination - clinically silent, and therefore not ruled out by a normal neurological examination - is why CNS assessment and treatment are handled as a mandatory part of first-line management rather than as a reaction to symptoms. A frequently quoted figure of roughly 30% occult involvement at diagnosis is not curated here: it traces to a source this session did not fetch.

nodes.description: Acquired resistance to tagraxofusp does not run through loss of the target. CD123 is retained; what the cell loses is the diphthamide biosynthesis pathway, silenced by DNA methylation, and diphthamide is the modified histidine residue the diphtheria-toxin moiety needs in order to ADP-ribosylate elongation factor 2. The drug still binds and still enters - it simply has nothing to act on. This is why a hypomethylating agent, which restores the pathway, is a rational partner rather than merely an additive cytotoxic.

Phylogenomic reconstruction places ultraviolet damage *before* the alterations associated with malignant transformation in at least some tumours - the source says UV damage "can precede" them, and BPDCN skin tumours appear first at sun-exposed anatomical sites carrying clonally expanded UV mutational signatures. The selection mechanism is lineage-specific: Tet2 loss of function confers resistance to UV-induced cell death in plasmacytoid but not conventional dendritic cells. The founder lesion therefore does more than permit transformation — it determines *where* the premalignant clone survives, which is why the disease presents in skin.

nodes.description: ZRSR2, an X-linked minor-spliceosome component, is recurrently inactivated in BPDCN and almost exclusively in males. The resulting intron retention prevents pDCs from upregulating IRF7 after inflammatory stimulation, so the cells neither activate nor undergo the apoptosis that normally follows activation. This is the best-supported mechanistic account of the disease's approximately 3:1 male predominance.
